shape.name: The wall in the wind
shape.beats: hook: the structure already moving the wrong way, named and dated, with the force that did it and the question how -> its nickname or reputation (it was already known to move) -> the design choice that made it vulnerable (flat cross-section: what the force meets) -> the motion changes kind on a word -> the turn: the loop where the motion feeds the force -> silence, the part gives way in cutaway -> the payoff: the piece lost and the toll, once -> the change it led to (the test, the new design) -> a pick-one between the old and new design -> loop to the first frame
shape.why: the cause is not a weak part but a shape meeting a force: a cross-section the wind can't pass through and a feedback loop carry it better than a cause chain of mistakes

title: Why Did the Tacoma Narrows Bridge Twist Itself Apart?
description:
The Tacoma Narrows Bridge tore itself apart in a steady wind, just months after it opened. How does wind do that to steel?
We rebuild Galloping Gertie in 3D from Washington State's history of the bridge: the solid side plates, the twist that fed itself, the piece of deck that fell into the Narrows, and the wind-tunnel testing that followed.
Sources: WSDOT, Tacoma Narrows Bridge history (Nov 1940).
Based on official investigation reports and published sources. 3D scenes are reconstructions, not actual footage.
